first.rationale: Verify the two most decision-relevant claims: whether promotional pricing produced sustainable qualified revenue rather than short-term, low-margin acquisition, and whether shorter onboarding improved downstream value beyond early adoption. I currently favor simplifying onboarding because completion and activation are both declining, while discounting carries unresolved retention, qualification, and margin risk.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified record directly addresses the current completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable value rather than only top-of-funnel lift. Promotional pricing is rejected because verification revealed 30-day retention fell 12% despite acquisition and qualified-revenue gains. Longer-term revenue impact beyond 30 days remains uncertain, so this should remain an experiment rather than a broad rollout.
